---
title: "Graph Representation 2"
subtitle: "Systematic Graph Traversal"
---

So far we randomly picked nodes from the bag to traverse the graph. While we are traversing, we can notice that we can do one of the following:

1. Explore the nodes IN THE ORDER we encounter them.

::: {.static-graph-inline}
<div id="order-encounter-graph"></div>
:::

2. Explore the nodes immediately adjacent to our current node first.

::: {.static-graph-inline}
<div id="order-adjacent-graph"></div>
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
import { mountStaticGraphView } from "./js/static-graph-view.js";

// A—B, A—D, A—E; B—C; C—F; D—G, D—H
sharedEdges = ([
  { id: "A—B", source: "A", target: "B" },
  { id: "A—D", source: "A", target: "D" },
  { id: "A—E", source: "A", target: "E" },
  { id: "B—C", source: "B", target: "C" },
  { id: "C—F", source: "C", target: "F" },
  { id: "D—G", source: "D", target: "G" },
  { id: "D—H", source: "D", target: "H" },
])

layout = ({
  E: { x: 170, y: 150 },
  A: { x: 60, y: 140 },
  B: { x: 150, y: 40 },
  C: { x: 250, y: 90 },
  F: { x: 350, y: 50 },
  D: { x: 150, y: 230 },
  G: { x: 250, y: 290 },
  H: { x: 250, y: 200 },
})

node = (id, order = null) => ({
  id,
  label: id,
  order,
  x: layout[id].x,
  y: layout[id].y,
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Encounter order from A: B then D (E still waiting). Path A→B→C marked.
encounterNodes = ([
  node("A", "1"),
  node("B", "2"),
  node("C"),
  node("D", "4"),
  node("E", "3"),
  node("F"),
  node("G"),
  node("H"),
])

encounterView = mountStaticGraphView(
  document.querySelector("#order-encounter-graph"),
  { nodes: encounterNodes, edges: sharedEdges },
  {
    width: 420,
    height: 340,
    directed: false,
    caption: "Visit order: A → B → D",
    highlight: {
      visited: ["A", "B", "D", "E"],
      pathEdges: ["A—B", "A—D", "A—E"],
    },
  }
);
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Go deep along neighbours first: A → B → C → F. Same path A→B→C marked.
adjacentNodes = ([
  node("A", "1"),
  node("B", "2"),
  node("C", "3"),
  node("D"),
  node("E"),
  node("F", "4"),
  node("G"),
  node("H"),
])

adjacentView = mountStaticGraphView(
  document.querySelector("#order-adjacent-graph"),
  { nodes: adjacentNodes, edges: sharedEdges },
  {
    width: 420,
    height: 340,
    directed: false,
    caption: "Visit order: A → B → C → F",
    highlight: {
      visited: ["A", "B", "C", "F"],
      pathEdges: ["A—B", "B—C", "C—F"],
    },
  }
);
```

### Exercise: Select the order

Let us explore the same traversal problem from the previous lecture in a different way. You are trapped back in the space station. Each room may have several doors leading to other rooms.This time your aim is to reach the Admin Room.

The graph on the left shows the rooms and paths. From the options, select the correct room order if you were to explore the graph using the two strategies above. 

#### Strategy 1

1. Explore one path completely. Pick the first door and keep walking through new rooms until you reach a room with no unexplored doors. Then backtrack to the previous room and try another door. Continue until you find Admin.

::: {.static-graph-inline}
<div id="dfs-quiz"></div>
:::

#### Strategy 2

2. Explore the rooms in the order we encounter them.

When we explore a single room, we would encounter its adjacent neighbours first. We would list them in the order we encounter them (but not enter them to see their further rooms). 

In other words: Search level by level. Enter a room, check whether it is the exit, and record every door leading to new room. But come back to the initial room and fully explore its adjacent rooms. Only then enter the deeper rooms.Repeat until you find Admin.

::: {.static-graph-inline}
<div id="bfs-quiz"></div>
:::


```{ojs}

      { id: "TH", label: "H", correct: false, feedback: "H was discovered one step after G (via D) — G goes first." },
      { id: "ADMIN", label: "Admin", correct: false, feedback: "Almost! Admin was just discovered, via F — it's last in line at level 3." },
    ],
    note: "Even though Admin is now visible, according to our algorithm we would visit G and H first since they were discovered earlier in the queue.",
  },
  {
    visible: V_ALL, current: "TG",
    pathEdgesBefore: ["CAF—MED", "CAF—ELEC", "CAF—STO", "MED—TA", "MED—TB", "ELEC—TD", "STO—TF", "TA—TG"], pathEdgesAfter: ["CAF—MED", "CAF—ELEC", "CAF—STO", "MED—TA", "MED—TB", "ELEC—TD", "STO—TF", "TA—TG", "TD—TH"],
    bagBefore: ["H","Admin"], bagAfter: ["Admin"],
    trackingBefore: ["Cafeteria", "MedBay", "Electrical", "Storage", "A", "B", "D", "F", "G"], trackingAfter: ["Cafeteria", "MedBay", "Electrical", "Storage", "A", "B", "D", "F", "G", "H"],
    prompt: "G has no further doors. Which room is next: H or Admin?",
    options: [
      { id: "TH", label: "H", correct: true, feedback: "H — discovered before Admin (via D, before F was visited)." },
      { id: "TA", label: "A", correct: false, feedback: "We already visited A" },
      { id: "MED", label: "MedBay", correct: false, feedback: "We already visited MedBay" },
    ],
    note: "One room left in the queue after this: Admin itself.",
  },
  {
    visible: V_ALL, current: "TH",
    pathEdgesBefore: ["CAF—MED", "CAF—ELEC", "CAF—STO", "MED—TA", "MED—TB", "ELEC—TD", "STO—TF", "TA—TG", "TD—TH"], pathEdgesAfter: ["CAF—MED", "CAF—ELEC", "CAF—STO", "MED—TA", "MED—TB", "ELEC—TD", "STO—TF", "TA—TG", "TD—TH", "TF—ADMIN"],
    bagBefore: ["Admin"], bagAfter: [],
    trackingBefore: ["Cafeteria", "MedBay", "Electrical", "Storage", "A", "B", "D", "F", "G", "H"], trackingAfter: ["Cafeteria", "MedBay", "Electrical", "Storage", "A", "B", "D", "F", "G", "H", "Admin"],
    prompt: "Only one room is left in the queue. Which is it?",
    options: [
      { id: "ADMIN", label: "Admin", correct: true, feedback: "Admin! The last room in the queue. BFS reaches the goal." },
      { id: "TG", label: "G", correct: false, feedback: "We already visited G" },
      { id: "TF", label: "F", correct: false, feedback: "We already visited F" },
    ],
    note: "Final order: Cafeteria → MedBay, Electrical, Storage → A, B, D, F → G, H, Admin. We visited every room level by level, instead of diving deep the way DFS does.",
  },
];

dfs_quiz_questions = buildQuizQuestions(dfs_steps);
bfs_quiz_questions = buildQuizQuestions(bfs_steps);

mountTraversalQuiz(document.querySelector("#dfs-quiz"), { questions: dfs_quiz_questions });
mountTraversalQuiz(document.querySelector("#bfs-quiz"), { questions: bfs_quiz_questions });
```

Now that we have an intuition for the two strategies, let us explore how we can implement them in code. How do we record the order? Careful observation reveals that for the first strategy, we fully explore the newest rooms we encounter first. While in the second one we explore the rooms in the order we encounter them. 

If we take another look at the "Bag" we can see that for the first strategy we are emptying the bag from right to left, and for the second one left to right. 

So instead of a set like last time, we can use a list to record the rooms we encounter. For the first strategy we can remove the last item after each iteration, while for the second one we can remove the first item. Hold on, is there a data structure for these two operations? Yes, it is a stack for the first strategy and a queue for the second one! 

### DIY

Make your own graph and then try to list the nodes in the order you would visit them using both strategies. For consistency: for selecting between nodes in the same room (like A and B in the previous example), use an alphabetical order to populate the bag. Thus when you pop from the bag, you would pop B before A for the first strategy (i.e. from the end of the list), and A before B for the second one (i.e. from the start of the list).

### Implement in code!

Drag the blocks to the right place to implement the first strategy. This is going to explore the latest rooms first. In other words, we are going to go to the very deep rooms, then start backtracking. Or do a Depth First Search (DFS).


```{ojs}
//| echo: false
heatCodeBlocks1 = mountCodeBlocksView(document.querySelector("#heat-code-blocks"), [
  { id: "pick", code: "node = bag.pop()", label: "pick the last node from the bag AND remove it simultaneously" },
  { id: "check_goal", code: "if node == \"Admin\":\n    goal_reached = True\n    break", label: "check if we reached the goal — stop if so" },
  { id: "track_neighbours", code: "neighbours = get_neighbours(node)\ntracking += neighbours", label: "track the current node's neighbours" },
  { id: "bag_neighbours", code: "bag += neighbours", label: "add the neighbours to the bag" },
], {
  heading: "Traversal Steps",
  workspaceLabel: "Loop body — while bag:",
  preplaced: [],
  solutionOrder: ["pick", "check_goal", "track_neighbours", "bag_neighbours"],
  lockedBefore: [
    { code: "bag = list()\ntracking = list()\n\ntracking.append(\"Cafeteria\")\nbag.append(\"Cafeteria\")\ngoal_reached = False" },
  ],
  lockedContainer: { code: "while bag:" },
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
heatCodeViz1 = mountHeatCodeViz(document.querySelector("#heat-code-viz"), {
  width: 420,
  height: 280,
  stepDelayMs: 900,
  data: createTraversalGraphData({ width: 420, height: 280 }),
  bagFooter: "ordered list — pop from the right (stack)",
  getPython: () => heatCodeBlocks1.toPython(),
  onStep: (frame) => {
    if (frame?.blockId) heatCodeBlocks1.highlight(frame.blockId);
    else heatCodeBlocks1.clearHighlight();
  },
})
```

For the second one, we are going to explore the room in the order we encounter them. We note this order in our list. In other words, we are going to explore the entire breadth first before going deeper. Or do a Breadth First Search (BFS).
